video.title: The Easiest Way to Start an Online Business (SaaS)

summary: Chris Koerner shows that dozens of businesses on HighLevel's awards page make $50k-$500k/month by white-labelling HighLevel's CRM for a single niche (insurance agents, clinics, gyms). He walks through a free reverse-engineering toolkit (Meta Ads Library, Wayback Machine, Similarweb, BuiltWith, LinkedIn Sales Navigator) to copy competitors' offers, ads and onboarding. Key takeaway: positioning one generic tool for one profession plus a killer offer is the business; sales and marketing are the hard part. He promotes his HighLevel affiliate link.

ideas.name: White-label GoHighLevel vertical SaaS (CRM for a niche)

ideas.problem: Generic CRMs like HubSpot/Salesforce are built for everyone; niche professionals prefer software positioned only for them
ideas.offer: A branded, niche-positioned CRM and marketing platform (built on HighLevel) with onboarding emails, setup calls and training materials, often with a 14-day free trial

acquisition.how: In the UK cold SMS/ringless voicemail to sole traders is illegal under PECR; cold email to limited companies and TPS/CTPS-screened calls possible; partnerships and paid ads need human deal-making. Inbound SEO/ads automate better.

onboarding.how: Welcome emails, snapshots and training can be templated in HighLevel; setup calls need a human or AI agent.

delivery.how: Software is HighLevel's; reseller only maintains templates.

support.how: Difficult clients and broken things need human support; AI helpdesk can cover tier 1.

uk_applicability.notes: HighLevel works in the UK and niche CRMs sell, but UK cold outreach is constrained by PECR (no cold SMS/voicemail drops to sole traders) and UK GDPR applies to client data the CRM stores; medical niches add data-protection obligations.

risks: Many resellers in same niches; competition
Revenue figures for 7 Figure Docs are AI estimates, not verified
Host earns affiliate commission on HighLevel sign-ups
UK PECR limits the outbound channels used by US resellers

tactics.name: Mine the HighLevel awards page for proven white-label businesses
steps: Open HighLevel's awards page (diamond/gold/platinum = 1,000/500/100 sub-accounts)
Give the URL to Claude and ask for companies that hit seven figures within a year
Have the AI search articles, LinkedIn and Reddit for each
Google each company's site, pricing and niche

quote.text: look at some of these company names and find me some that reach seven figures in a year or less
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Find winning ads in the Meta Ads Library
steps: Search all ads by keyword, company or geography
Filter end date to ads running for 4+ months (long-running = profitable)
Prefer advertisers with many long-running ads (sign of scale)
Screenshot and give to an AI agent (Manus, ChatGPT Operator) to find which run on HighLevel
Copy the ad, changing as little as possible
Use UK listing to see spend disclosures

quote.text: if you see an ad that has been up for months then it is a banger ad and you should copy everything about that ad and change as little as possible
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Reverse-engineer a competitor with Wayback Machine, Similarweb and BuiltWith
steps: Wayback Machine: see launch pricing, headline and offer (e.g. Agent CRM $47 -> $97, 14-day trial kept)
Similarweb (free account): weekly visits and traffic sources to infer outbound vs ads vs SEO
BuiltWith Chrome extension: see payments, pixels, ClickFunnels/HighLevel
LinkedIn Sales Navigator 30-day trial (cancel immediately) to see which industries and company sizes they serve

quote.text: what did their website look like when they first launched because that's going to save us x number of years of heartache and trial and error
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Launch your white-label in a 30-day trial window
steps: Start HighLevel white-label trial (30 days via affiliate link vs 14 standard)
AI-generated logo and colours
Pick a niche by passion/experience or ask ChatGPT which awards-page industry has least competition
Copy proven ad angles, pricing, offer and site structure
Copy onboarding: welcome emails, setup calls, training materials
Get prospects on the phone before the trial ends
Upgrade to $500 unlimited plan only once revenue covers it

quote.text: step three copy their proven ad angles their pricing their offer the structure of their website everything do not try to reinvent the wheel
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Rent someone else's BuiltWith account via Upwork
steps: Post a $20-$50 Upwork job for someone with a BuiltWith subscription
Ask them to export a list (e.g. Shopify or HighLevel sites)

warnings.warning: This is active work, not passive income: you must learn sales and marketing and handle difficult clients.

quote.text: this isn't your passive income make money while you sleep bull crap this is going to be work
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Most Facebook ads are killed within days; only copy ads that have run for months.

quote.text: it's very common to kill an ad after just a couple days because they aren't performing
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Avoid analysis paralysis: research one company for a week then talk to customers.

quote.text: do the hard thing not the easy thing of just researching until you're glue in the face analysis paralysis to the gills
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Revenue estimates come from AI searches and back-of-napkin maths, not verified data.
UK: the outbound text/ringless voicemail tactics inferred for US resellers breach PECR if aimed at individuals or sole traders without consent; screen calls against TPS/CTPS.

lessons.lesson: Positioning a horizontal tool for one profession beats competing as a generic product.

quote.text: it's positioning and framing cuz if you're an insurance agent are you more likely to go buy HubSpot
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: The key to scaling is an offer people feel stupid saying no to; copy it from proven competitors.

quote.text: the key to scaling a big business is having a killer offer an offer that people feel stupid saying no to
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Long-running ads in the Meta Ads Library reveal what is profitable.
Traffic-source mix (Similarweb) tells you whether a competitor grows by outbound, ads or SEO.
Outbound is faster than waiting for SEO and cheaper than heavy paid ads.

quote.text: I am way too impatient to wait for SEO to work and I'm way too cheap to pour thousands of dollars a day into Facebook or Google ads
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Scale platform costs only when revenue covers them.

quote.text: you don't have to commit to that until you have enough customers that are paying you at least $500 a month
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Onboarding (welcome emails, setup calls, training) is a core part of what to copy.
Partnering with a franchisor can deliver hundreds of customers at once.

evidence_quality.rationale: Second-hand research of other companies; revenues are AI-sourced or back-of-napkin estimates. Tool walkthrough is concrete.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris promotes his HighLevel affiliate link.
